title: The Crooked Wolf Revisited
premise: Tamsin Thornbury, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Vael, discovers her name and tonight's date in a century-old prophecy hidden in a smuggler's cache. The prophecy names her as either the Crooked Wolf who frees the true king Aldric from the usurper's crown-spirit, or the wolf who devours him. Guided by a disgraced archivist and the king's estranged daughter, Tamsin crosses Thornfell as the usurper's armies march on the free cities. In the end she learns Vael's silence was a sacrifice — the god poured itself into her oath to keep the crown-spirit caged — and by speaking her truth and breaking her own oath, she unbinds both king and god, choosing her found family over destiny.
about_author: Rosalind Nakamura is a former mountain guide who traded trail maps for story maps after a winter stranded in a fire lookout with nothing but a battered anthology of folklore. She writes fantasy about people whose loyalties cost them something, and still cannot resist a good smuggler's pass.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Taking shelter in an abandoned waystation, she finds a prophecy book naming her and tonight's date. A crown-shaped shadow passes overhead; the first usurper scouts reach the pass. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve — she has never believed in gods or fate, but someone wrote her down.

chapters.title: Oath of a Silent God
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Flashbacks interleave with the present as she traces the prophecy's origin to Archivist Wren Calloway, exiled for reading forbidden texts. Wren reveals the prophecy offers two endings: liberator or devourer. Emotional beat: Tamsin confronts how much of her identity is the oath itself.

chapters.title: The King in the Gilded Cage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Infiltrating the capital, they witness King Aldric — lucid for moments only — begging a servant to cut off his own crowned head. The usurper General Mavros senses intruders. Emotional beat: horror and pity; the enemy is not a man but a thing wearing one.

chapters.title: Daughter of Two Crowns
chapters.summary: Sera's POV (the king's daughter). Sera intercepts Tamsin and Wren, testing them with blades before trust. She knows the crown-spirit's weakness lies in Thornfell's deepest shrine — where Vael went silent. Emotional beat: prickly alliance forming into the seed of found family.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Fleeing Mavros's riders through the mountains she knows best, Tamsin leads them along roads that shouldn't exist. An ambush costs them their supplies and nearly Sera's life. Emotional beat: Tamsin realizes she'd trade any secret road for these two people's safety.

chapters.title: What the Shrine Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At Vael's silent shrine, the prophecy's second half surfaces: the god did not die — it was spent, poured into an oath to cage the crown-spirit. Every sworn mercenary carries a fragment. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes Tamsin's whole life as a vessel, not a person.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Mercy
chapters.summary: Mavros's POV. The general offers Tamsin a pardon and her old company back if she delivers Sera. He shows her the free cities' armies burning — proof resistance is doomed. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by grief; loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Broken Oaths
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She refuses Mavros and fights free, but breaking faith with her employer shatters part of her oath-fragment — and with it, the cage holding the crown-spirit weakens. Sera learns Tamsin may be the devourer after all. Emotional beat: betrayal, guilt, and the terror of being the prophecy's villain.

chapters.title: The Crooked Wolf
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. As Mavros's armies breach the free cities' last wall, Tamsin enters Aldric's mind through her oath-bond, speaks her full truth aloud, and renounces the oath entirely — releasing Vael, who tears the crown-spirit loose. Climax: she chooses self-defined identity over written fate, at the edge of death.

chapters.title: A Crown of Her Own Choosing
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Aldric, freed, abdicates to Sera rather than rule a kingdom that watched him suffer. Vael, reborn and wordless, marks Tamsin not with an oath but a choice renewed each day. The found family rides out together. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging freely given, never sworn.
